executive_summary: Round 2: REVISE. Independent sha256sum confirms candidate SHA-256 b732a4b7c39234b7ac9262fef29a45361c3dd190898fcb38cc44f1f8c21b70d6. The four round-1 corrections are substantively reflected in the prose and page: the two midpoint differences recompute to 2 bp and 12.5 bp, the Michigan rank superlative is gone from claim-bearing text, and the Fed pricing source date is Sep 28. Live official policy checks confirm the Sep 16 Fed action/range/vote and next FOMC dates (https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260916a.htm; https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm), plus the BoC 2.25% setting and Oct 28/Dec 9 decision dates (https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2026/09/fad-press-release-2026-09-02/; https://www.bankofcanada.ca/core-functions/monetary-policy/key-interest-rate/). All 97 SHA-256 fields with evidence bindings match disk; the retrieval manifest hash matches and its 38 entries record the relevant refresh failures. I recomputed all six Yahoo ticker 1d/1w moves and all six driver-window returns from raw captures; only Monday Sep 28 close prices are claimed. The structural gate passed 13/13 with brief regeneration true; render tests passed 5/5, full tests passed 65/65, and an isolated Chrome dump showed the monthly Fed label, quarterly BoC label, both panels, neutral NO TRADE / NO EDGE status, no fabricated odds, and the requested brief sections. The staged latest.json was restored byte-for-byte and its git status is empty. One major inconsistency remains in the frozen payload: ZQV26's 3.895% is still stored under a quarterly-named field, contradicting the tenor correction and its metadata. The displayed page label is correct, but the underlying claim-bearing field is not; therefore publication is not approved.

findings.issue: Iteration-02 did not fully clear the Fed tenor finding: it stores ZQV26's 3.895% at the claim-bearing key implied_quarterly_average_rate, incorrectly assigning a quarterly horizon to an October 30-day average. This also contradicts the metadata claims that ZQV26 is labeled monthly 'everywhere' and 'throughout the payload'. The page's rate_label renders correctly, but the candidate JSON remains semantically inconsistent.
findings.evidence: On-disk candidate.json at meetings.fed.pricing.observable_proxy.implied_quarterly_average_rate contains 3.895; the adjacent instrument, contract_horizon_caveat, note, and rate_label identify the October monthly/30-day average. CME's official 30-Day Fed Funds rule states final settlement is 100 minus the arithmetic average of daily EFFR during the contract delivery month (https://www.cmegroup.com/tools-information/lookups/advisories/ser/SER-7594.pdf). The renderer at fed-boc-watcher/index.html lines 1029-1030 reads the quarterly-named property and appends rate_label; my headless Chrome dump confirmed the visible Fed text is '3.895% October monthly (30-day) average EFFR'. Thus this is a payload/metadata contradiction, not a visible-page labeling failure.
findings.pnl_impact: A downstream reader or calculation that consumes the payload key can treat a one-month EFFR exposure as a quarterly average, misstate the contract horizon and hedge sensitivity around Oct 28, and size on the wrong tenor. The current rendered card is correctly labeled, which limits immediate reader risk but does not cure the frozen payload's semantics.
